subject: Pricing bucket rebalance + bundling package — redline review
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@bundletech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing bucket rebalance + bundling package — redline review

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As promised I’m attaching a proposed revision to Exhibit B that reflects the bucket rebalancing we discussed (move from three coarse tiers to five usage buckets) and an optional bundling package for endpoint + embeddings that gives a blended discount at scale. Key highlights: 

- New bucket structure (0-10k / 10k-50k / 50k-200k / 200k-1M / 1M+ tokens) with stepped unit pricing.
- Bundling package: 10% off for combined endpoint+embedding volume once combined monthly usage > 150k tokens.
- Minimum commitment clause: we propose annual minimum = prior-year committed spend (PYCS) less 10% for year 1, with quarterly true-ups.
- Floor on unit price: no below-60% of current base rate unless customer moves to Dedicated.

I attached the updated Exhibit B (20270630-exhibitB-proposal.pdf) and a pricing-bucket-matrix-v2.xlsx for reference. Please have your legal team mark up Exhibit B where needed — we tried to keep the guardrails tight so this is billable predictable economics for you while giving BundleTech upside for packaging.

Can you confirm whether the bundling discount should apply to committed volume only or to any combined usage (committed + overage)? If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up this week to run through the matrix.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: 20270630-exhibitB-proposal.pdf (pdf), pricing-bucket-matrix-v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@bundletech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: BundleTech Legal <legal@bundletech.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing bucket rebalance + bundling package — redline review

Jordan —

Thanks for sending these over. Legal placed a first-pass markup (attached: BundleTech_redlines_20270630.docx) and procurement had a few commercial asks. High level:

1) Annual minimum: we can accept a move to buckets, but need a floor that preserves ~70% of our current commitment for year 1 (we can discuss stepping down in year 2).
2) Bundling discount scope: we prefer the discount to apply to committed volume only (not to unpredictable overages) for the first 12 months.
3) True-up cadence: quarterly sounds fine, but need the true-up cap on billing adjustments per quarter to be no more than 20% to avoid cashflow volatility.
4) Price protection: we want a 12-month rate hold after signing on finalized Exhibit B (no unit price increases for 12 months).

Please see the redline file — we added alternative language around the annual minimum formula (Section 2.1) and suggested explicit examples for how bundling is calculated (Section 4). Also included a DocuSign template link for faster turnaround if you want to move to signature.

We’re generally aligned but need a little tightening on protections before we can commit. Can we get a short internal confirmation from Redwood on the floor and the bundling scope today? If so, happy to book a legal/finance sync tomorrow morning.

Regards,

Maya Singh
Head of Procurement | BundleTech Inc.
maya.singh@bundletech.com | +1 212-555-0183

Attachment: BundleTech_redlines_20270630.docx (docx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing bucket rebalance + bundling package — redline review

Forwarding Maya’s redlines and commercial asks. Quick internal note on concessions I’m willing to authorize without exec escalation:

- Annual minimum: accept PYCS - 10% in contract language, but we can offer an alternate commercial path to 70% if they sign a 12-month committed seat for Dedicated or take a minimum guaranteed throughput. Prefer to keep the contractual floor at -10% to avoid precedent.
- Bundling discount: agree to committed-volume-only for first 12 months, then revisit. This limits cost exposure while giving them commercial benefit.
- True-up cap: can accept a 25% cap per quarter as a compromise (their ask 20%).
- Rate hold: agree to 12-month rate hold post-signature — discretionary.

Ask legal to prepare a short addendum that: (a) defines PYCS calculation explicitly, (b) adds a worked example for bundling math, (c) inserts a quarterly true-up cap clause. Neha — can you draft that addendum and review the redline doc? Jordan — please confirm whether we want to offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset perceived downside of the floor. If yes, keep it under $25k and make it conditional on signature within 14 days.

Karthik
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
